title.narrative: World Bank Trust Fund Cash Transfers

description.narrative:
Stöd under 2019-2022 med totalt 75 miljoner SEK till utbyggnad av nationella sociala kontantstöd via Världsbankens Multi Donor Trust Fund, med fokus på att registrera fler förmånstagare, öka bidragsbeloppen (socialbidrag, barnbidrag, beredskapsarbete m.m.) samt stärka kapaciteten på socialförsäkringsmyndigheten INAS. Total budget för programmet är ca 180 miljoner SEK och andra givare är Storbritannien och Nederländerna. Det svenska bidraget uppgår till ca 41 procent an total budget. Fonden är aktiv sedan slutet av 2018.
Insatsen förväntas bidra till effektiva och transparenta utbetalningar samt till att vidareutveckla registret över förmånstagare (e-INAS ). Stödet är ett av de insatser i den svenska portföljen som tydligt kommer att svara mot de effekter som cyklonen IDAI medfört i de centrala delarna av landet. Minst 18 500 hushåll kommer att nås av insatsen, en siffra som kan komma att öka dramatiskt då fler givare kommer in med särskilt stöd till cyklondrabbade områden.

Support during 2019-2022 with a total sum of 75 million SEK to scale-up the national social cash transfer system through a World Bank Multi Donor Trust Fund. Total budget is ca 180 million SEK, and other donors are UK and the Netherlands. Swedish share around 41 percent of total budget. The fund is active since end of 2018.
Focus is on scaling up cash transfers (social cash transfers, child grant, public works salaries) and on increasing the number of beneficiaries. The contribution is expected to strengthen INAS, the agency for social security, assure an efficient and transparent payment system and develop the beneficary registry (e-INAS). The support is one of the contributions that will reply to the negative effects of the cyclone IDAI in the central parts of the country.
At least 18 500 households will be reached by the intervention, a number toat may increase dramatically as more donors are coming in with specific support to mitigate for the effects of the cyclones.

The Multi-Donor Trust Fund Strengthening Mozambiques Social Protection System (MozSP MDTF) supports the scale up of Social protection coverage and strengthen delivery systems through a pooled funding approach for donor partner engagement in the SP sector in Mozambique.
The development objective of the MozSP is to strengthen the social protection system in Mozambique and it is designed to:
(i) increased coverage of poor households; (ii) generate knowledge and evidence-based instruments that improve efficiency of existing SP systems; and (iii) enhanced coordination with development partners.
The MozSP finances grants which contribute to the achievement of these objectives, these are structured in two pillars: Recipient-Executed activities (RETF): implemented by the Government of Mozambique (GoM) through Ministry of Labour, Gender and Social Action (MTGAS) and National Institute of Social Action (INAS).These activities are designed to strengthen coverage of existing social protection programs, prioritize income support to eligible households in existing Social Protection programs by financing existing income support cash transfers, associated implementation costs, and piloting and scaling up solutions that enhance the efficiency and impact of SP programs.
Bank-Executed activities (BETF): implemented by WB, including through local and international individual consultants as well as firms. These activities finance the provision of technical assistance to contribute to the knowledge generation, development and testing of innovative solutions to improve the functioning of SP systems in the following areas (i) strengthening the delivery systems of existing social programs, (ii) enhancing intersectoral synergies; and (iii) improving coordination and integration of the SP system. The BETF activities are designed to complement and support the implementation of the WB SPER project and other WB projects1 in the Human Development sector

title.narrative: Agreement amendment Strengthening Mozambique Social Protection System

description.narrative:
1. Strengthened Mozambique's social protection delivery systems through digital transformation The contribution supported the continued strengthening of the e-INAS Management Information System, improving beneficiary management, payment processing, data quality, interoperability and system functionality. The completion of the SPARKS-IT assessment provided a comprehensive roadmap for the modernization of Mozambique's social protection information system, strengthening the foundations for more efficient and transparent programme delivery.
2. Advanced the development of a Unified Social Registry (Cadastro Social Único) The programme supported the Government in launching the development of a Unified Social Registry, representing an important milestone towards a more integrated, transparent and efficient social protection system. National consultations were conducted, an inter-ministerial technical working group was established and a roadmap for implementation was initiated to strengthen beneficiary identification, programme targeting and interoperability across government systems.
3. Expanded digital Government-to-Person (G2P) payments The contribution supported the transition towards digital social protection payments, improving transparency, accountability and financial inclusion. By October 2025, more than 125,800 beneficiaries had received benefits through digital payment mechanisms. New decentralized payment models and alternative payment platforms were successfully piloted to improve efficiency, reduce payment delays and strengthen the resilience of the national payment system.
4. Strengthened institutional capacity and governance of Mozambique's social protection system The programme strengthened the institutional and operational capacity of the Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Action (MTGAS) and the National Institute for Social Action (INAS) through improvements in financial management, procurement, planning and programme implementation. Capacity development included training 173 government staff in financial management and procurement, alongside technical training on environmental and social safeguards, adaptive social protection and gender-based violence (GBV). Investments in ICT equipment and operational infrastructure further strengthened institutional performance.
5. Improved efficiency, coverage and resilience of national social protection programmes The contribution strengthened implementation of key national social protection programmes, including the Basic Social Subsidy Programme (PSSB), the Child Grant and the Productive Social Action Programme (PASP). Improved beneficiary targeting, strengthened case management, expanded digital delivery mechanisms and enhanced operational systems contributed to more effective programme implementation.
6. Strengthened programme delivery through strategic implementation partnerships To improve implementation efficiency and accelerate programme delivery, the programme established strategic implementation partnerships with the World Food Programme (WFP) and Give Directly for the implementation of the Productive Social Action Programme (PASP). These partnerships expanded programme delivery in cyclone-affected districts and strengthened the Government's capacity to reach vulnerable households more effectively.
7. Strengthened Mozambique's shock-responsive social protection system The contribution enhanced the Government's capacity to respond to crises through strengthened shock-responsive social protection mechanisms. Emergency cash transfer programmes (PASD-PE) were expanded, digital payment systems improved, and preparedness strengthened to respond to Cyclones Chido, Dikeledi and Jude, contributing to a more resilient national social protection system.
8. Strengthened evidence-based policy development and future social protection reforms The programme generated strategic analytical work to inform national social protection reforms, including support for the development of the National Basic Social Security Strategy III (ENSSB III), the review of the Proxy Means Test (PMT), assessment of the e-INAS platform (SPARKS-IT), impact evaluations and analytical work on integrated social protection systems. These investments strengthened the evidence base for future policy decisions and sector reforms.
9. Strengthened donor coordination and strategic dialogue The MDTF continued to serve as an important platform for harmonizing donor support and strengthening policy dialogue between Government and development partners. The programme supported improvements in the Social Protection Partners Group (SPPG), strengthened coordination mechanisms and contributed to aligning partner support around national priorities for social protection systems strengthening.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
